_about: ENHANCEMENT E16: the on-screen touch controls' look and layout, read by game/render/TouchControls (which has the same values built in, for when this file is missing or a field is). Replacing the art is a data-only change: put the new PNGs anywhere under game/data, point 'image' at them and adjust 'size' (what each is drawn at, stretched: an image needs at least that many pixels, in the same proportions) and the placement. Keep straight alpha and no exact magenta #FF00FF (the HUD keys it out). Units are the pixels of a logical screen 768 tall (1024 wide in the menus and in 4:3 levels, wider in widescreen levels), so sizes here are relative to the screen's height; E25's zoomed levels and a phone's larger menu draw the screen at another scale, and the controls are scaled with it so they keep their size on the window. 'anchor' is the corner of the safe area a control hangs from and 'offset' the distance from that corner to its nearest edges, inward; 'overhang' ([x, y], default none) is how far the control may lie past the safe area's edges it hangs from, and its offset may then be negative that far (never more than half the control's size). 'hitPadding' is how far past its edge a finger still lands on it; 'shape' (circle or rect) is its touch area. 'scale' multiplies every size, offset and padding. Alphas are 0..1: 'idleAlpha' at rest, 'pressedAlpha' while held. A control with "enabled": false is not there at all (a layout without the combo buttons, say); one left out of this file keeps its built-in place and image. The first, placeholder look is images/touch/placeholder/touch_controls.json: copy it over this file to go back to it.
_provenance: The buttons are Magic Rampage's screen pad (Magic Rampage 7.8.7, Asantee Games), made by tools/art/make_mr_touch_art.py from its package: images/touch/README.md says which image is which of its files and what was composed. Its buttons are 128 px squares (a 100 px face in a soft shadow), so they are touched as squares and drawn at 100-126. The layout is the port's own: the direction control under the left thumb with its buttons 25 units under the bottom row of the action buttons (E32; before it they were level with the sword button), left and right only, and E25's down button above them only where down takes the wizard on; since E32 the actions under the right thumb as a grid of two columns of three, set well in from the screen's right edge (the right column's edge 117 from it, not the corner's 24) with 67 units between the two columns of 120, a wider gap between neighbouring buttons (the widest the direction control's box allows on a 4:3 screen narrowed by a notch's two cut-outs: the left column's far edge, 304 + 120 from the right, is then the box's, 24 + 400 from the left), and the rows level, no stagger: from the bottom, the left column is the sword, its combo and the light, the right column the jump, the spell combo and the fire, the three rows 136 apart centre to centre (each combo, 100 wide, is centred in its column of 120); E29 had the columns 16 units apart with the cluster's edge 24 from the screen's and the right column 30 units higher; before E29 the four buttons were laid out as E3 maps a pad's face buttons (A jump at the bottom, X sword left, B fire right, Y light top) with the two combo buttons in a row above them; pause and back in the top-right corner below the run's timer (setupScene.as:337 draws it at (W-50, 0)), clear of the player status frames at the top-left (interface.as). Keys starting with '_' are notes.

dpad._note: Left and right (K_LEFT, K_RIGHT); no up, which only jumps, and since E25 no down: 'downSector' true gives it E16's down sector back (down within 67.5 degrees of straight down), with the down arrow 'arrows.down' images/touch/dpad_down.png, and exitDown's 'enabled' false takes the down button away - the layout before E25. That disc's down arrow is drawn below its centre, so it also wants the box back on the screen: 'offset' [24, 24] and no 'overhang'. One round control the thumb slides on without lifting; 'deadZone' is the fraction of the radius at the centre that means nothing. Its look is Magic Rampage's buttons: the arrows are each a whole button alone on a canvas the size of the control, where its direction's sector is (tools/art/make_mr_touch_art.py checks that every pixel of the left and right buttons is that direction alone), each brightened while its direction is held; the base image is empty (Magic Rampage has no disc). The knob, Magic Rampage's focus brackets, follows the thumb onto the button it holds; 'atRest' false draws nothing there while no thumb points a direction, since the brackets at the centre would frame the empty gap between the left and right buttons like a missing button (true keeps the knob at the centre, as the placeholder look's disc has it). The two buttons are drawn 21.7 units above the disc's centre and its lower half is empty, so the box hangs 138 units below the bottom edge ('offset' y -138, within 'overhang' 150): the buttons' centres are then 200 - 138 + 21.7 = 83.7 above the edge, 25 under the bottom row of the action buttons' (49 + 60 = 109, E32), while the disc, its dead zone, sectors and hit area are the same as when the box sat on the screen; a finger anywhere on the part of the disc that shows is on it. The box is 400 units, the art's 406 px at 0.985 units a pixel: each button is 126 units across with a face of about 118, as large as the action buttons

jump._note: K_CTRL (getJumpButtonStatus, playerInput.as:176). E32: the bottom of the right column, the right-most button, level with the sword button, its edge 117 from the screen's (E29: 24 from it and 30 higher than the sword button).

sword._note: K_S (getAttack01ButtonStatus, playerInput.as:201). E32: the bottom of the left column, 67 left of the right one, its edge 304 from the screen's (so that its box does not overlap the direction control's on a 4:3 screen narrowed by a notch's two cut-outs: 848 wide, 24 + 400 and 120 + 304 across); the sword combo and the light are above it (E29: 16 left of the jump button, 24 up from the bottom edge).

fire._note: K_D (getAttack02ButtonStatus, playerInput.as:221). E32: the top of the right column, above the spell combo, which is above the jump button; 272 above it, the rows being 136 apart.

light._note: K_SPACE (getAttack03ButtonStatus, playerInput.as:241). E32: the top of the left column, above the sword combo, which is above the sword button; level with the fire button.

swordCombo._note: The sword combo as a macro of player 1's keys, one a tick: the way the wizard faces, again after a release, then K_S (CMD side, side, SWORD; playerInput.as:361). Waits first, if need be, for the combo buffer to empty (210 ms without a press, combo.as:116). E32: the middle of the left column, between the sword button and the light, 10 further in than they are so that its 100 is centred over their 120, and halfway up between them (26 clear of each, the three rows 136 apart centre to centre).

spellCombo._note: The spell combo as a macro: K_DOWN, the way the wizard faces, then K_D (CMD DOWN, side, SPELL; playerInput.as:380). E32: the middle of the right column, between the jump button and the fire, centred over their 120 as the sword combo is over its column, and level with it.

exitDown._note: ENHANCEMENT E25: K_DOWN, shown only while the next_level door offers player 1 the way on (main.as:204-208, the scripts' g_nextLevelOffered) - the one place in play where down alone does anything. The arrows' size (126), centred over the gap between the left and right buttons (the disc's centre, 24 + 200 across) and about 17 units above their faces: x 161-287, y 482-608 of a 768-tall screen (the disc's centre is 768 + 138 - 200 = 706 down, the buttons' centres 21.7 above it, their faces' tops 59 above those). Its image is the disc's former down arrow, alone (tools/art/make_mr_touch_art.py).

pause._note: K_ESC in a level or an arena: E13's pause. Magic Rampage's pause is a pill, 128x86.

back._note: K_ESC in the arena select, game over and the end screens: back to the menu (waitForInputToMenu, escToGoToMenu). Hidden in the main menu, in the options (the original's own Back arrow is there, clicked by a finger) and in the pause.
